### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/rest`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via excludeSubmitter (literal, a string literal in SubmitterApprovalRefusal; a string literal in decideNode; a string literal in submitterRefusalUserMessage))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via excludeSubmitter (literal, a string literal in SubmitterApprovalRefusal; a string literal in decideNode; a string literal in submitterRefusalUserMessage))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c2e34cdb2b436f356ebba523e284e239f6ea351` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dc3dc14d5f1680d517d9195a6606c20d665b05cb` — the merge of head `a6c6666adee23afc20e585b0cc95a3fea78c0ed1` into base `5c2e34cdb2b436f356ebba523e284e239f6ea351`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dc3dc14d5f1680d517d9195a6606c20d665b05cb && git checkout dc3dc14d5f1680d517d9195a6606c20d665b05cb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5c2e34cdb2b436f356ebba523e284e239f6ea351 a6c6666adee23afc20e585b0cc95a3fea78c0ed1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5c2e34cdb2b436f356ebba523e284e239f6ea351 && git merge --no-ff a6c6666adee23afc20e585b0cc95a3fea78c0ed1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c2e34cdb2b436f356ebba523e284e239f6ea351
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5c2e34cdb2b436f356ebba523e284e239f6ea351` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — REWORK · repo:objectstack#3 · head 869d5de0 · 2026-11-24T04:59Z

L1: REWORK
Head-sha: `869d5de0ab657337f689ead79df7f9700cb0ef9d`
Card: #36463 (epic #36243) · claim 7121106831 · os-dev-report 7122061191 (`Dev-effort: high`, `Rounds: 1`).

### Checklist
- **Shape:** `l1-face` CLEAN, 13 items. Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #36463`, no closing keyword next to another card. `mergeable_state` clean.
- **Checks at this head:** 52 success, 10 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending. Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check and Type Check UI: success. The local UI type-check was NOT MEASURED in the report, and CI answers it.
- **Governance:** `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 36846`: NOT governed, 623 lines.
- **Changeset:** plugin-approvals, rest and console, all at patch. Each package is published or touched, and its touched files ship. The prose, read sentence by sentence:
  - the decide refusal: true. Both `FORBIDDEN` refusals still build their English `message` byte for byte from the same strings; only the throw moved into `refuseOwnApproval`;
  - the REST door: true (`approvals-routes.ts` +11 lines), with a control for unmarked and blank values;
  - the console: true (`flowResponse.ts` `refusalBodyUserMessage`, `ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx` `humanizeError`);
  - the submitter notice: true, with the cap of 8 stated.
- **Premise and route:** maintainer ruling 2026-11-17 option B is kept: the same predicates refuse, and only the text moved. The dispatch assumed the slots could be flattened into one param; the report measured the messaging layer and showed that cannot work (a keyed param is one hole-free key). The route it took instead, sentences derived per pack, is sound: nothing is translated twice, and every pack and size 2 to 8 is pinned.
- **Scope:** inside the claim surface. The claim named "the console reader that shows the decide refusal"; the diff touches two of them, record page and Approval Center, both declared in `deviations` and both direct consequences. `approval-notification-text.ts` was not needed and was not touched.
- **Tests:** real commands with output. plugin-approvals: 127 files, 1899 tests. rest: 433 files, 9114 tests. UI: 2 files, 17 tests. Two ablations turned red: deleting the mapper spread turned 1 test red, and voiding the service's `userMessage` turned 2 red. Both restore lines were pinned to the HEAD blob.

### Findings
**S1 (should-fix) — `Clause-②` declares `no`, but the approvals door's response body gains a member.**
`packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts:313` now puts `userMessage` at the top level of the flat `{ code, error }` refusal body. It does this for both decide refusals and, as written ("status-agnostic"), for every mapped row whose thrown error carries a marking. A door's response is part of the published contract that `Clause-②` declares (ADR-0150 §Clause-②: "spec, protocol, SDK, a door's request or response").
This repository's precedent for exactly this shape is `yes (widening)`:
- #34619 (`62d9d0d998`) added the same top-level `userMessage` to this same door's `RESUME_FAILED` body and declared `Clause-②: yes (widening)`;
- #35811 (`a8126d244d`) added `failedOperation` to the batch door's refusal body, with no type export moving, and declared `yes (widening)`.
That `ApiErrorSchema` already declares `userMessage`, and that `@objectstack/client` already lifts it, makes the change additive. Additive is the widening arm, not `no`.
**Fix:** in the changeset and the PR body, change the line to `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and add one paragraph naming the widened body:
  - which door and member;
  - which rows answer it today, the two decide refusals, and that it is absent when no producer marked one.
`Metadata-protocol: none` and patch stay (AGENTS.md Post-Task item 3: a non-protocol widening ships patch). Amend the claim's `Clause-②:` line on the card as paper.
**Consequence:** with `yes`, the PR carries the declaration face, which owes an L2 at `TIER_DEFAULT`. I have claimed and started it on this head (claim 7122485541). It will be re-read against the fixed head, so you do not need to request anything.

Nits:
- **N1:** a slate of more than 8 slots still names its slots in English. The report lists this with `carrier: none`, but it sits inside the card's own Acceptance ("a multi-slot submitter notice reads entirely in Chinese"). `Fixes` stays right, because the limit sits in `service-messaging`, outside this card's surface. **To the seat:** file a carrier card (a list-shaped keyed param in service-messaging), or record a decision not to.
- **N2:** the report's second out-of-scope observation (the Approval Center bulk approve names failures by record title only, with no reason) also has no carrier. **To the seat**, the same choice.

### Landing notes
After the fix: the delta L1 and the L2 record on the same head, then the area lands. `Fixes #36463` closes the card.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `869d5de0ab657337f689ead79df7f9700cb0ef9d`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #36463 (body and all four comments: triage 7080090045, unlock 7107672290, claim 7121106831, dev report 7122061191), the PR #36846 body and file list (13 files), the net diff `origin/main...869d5de0a`, and the check-runs on this head (62 runs: every one `success` or `skipped`, none failed or pending). Precedents were read off `main` with `git log -S`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **J1. Approvals REST door, wire body: a widening. The behaviour is right; the declaration is wrong (F1).** `handleApprovalError` in `packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts` now adds an optional top-level `userMessage` member to the flat `{ code, error }` body. It does so on every mapped row (`400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, `409 DUPLICATE_REQUEST` / `INVALID_STATE` / `RESUME_TARGET_LOST`, `429 THROTTLED`, `403 FORBIDDEN`, `404 REQUEST_NOT_FOUND`, `500 RESUME_FAILED` / `READ_BACK_FAILED`) whenever the thrown error carries a marking that `declaredUserMessage` accepts. Before this head the member appeared only on `RESUME_FAILED`, through the stranded spread. So the change adds a member to a public response body: it widens the public surface. The shape is correct:
  - The member is presence-gated. Blank and unmarked errors add nothing, and the control test pins this.
  - It matches `ApiErrorSchema.userMessage`, which is status-agnostic and never replaces `message`.
  - `@objectstack/client` already lifts it (`errorBody?.userMessage`).
  - The `RESUME_FAILED` stranded spread still comes last, so the #13807 / #34579 envelope keeps its own `userMessage`.
  - The code-anchored prefix strip from the 2026-08-31 ruling is untouched.
  - Today's in-tree producers are only the two decide refusals, both `403 FORBIDDEN`. The plugin's other marked errors (`lockedError` with its `RECORD_LOCKED:` prefix, and `snapshotQueryRefusal` with its `[Security]` prefix) match no mapping row. They still fall through to the `/data` classification arm, so their wire answer does not move.
- **J2. `ApprovalService.decide` thrown error: additive and correct.** Both refusals of a submitter's own approval (`excludeSubmitter`, and the override under `[Maintainer ruling 2026-11-17, option B]`) still refuse. Their `message` is byte-identical, and the existing English pins are unchanged. They gain `userMessage`, composed in the service from `readerLabels(context).sentence`. When the reader has no language, or the pack lacks a sentence, the whole text falls back to English. It never mixes the two languages and never names a user id. This holds the contract's "composed where it is produced" clause.
- **J3. Error-code surface: unchanged, which is right.** No new code is introduced, and `FORBIDDEN` was already registered. `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` / `StandardErrorCode` are untouched.
- **J4. Approvals translation catalog: added keys, `Clause-②: no` by precedent. Right.** The PR adds five authored `approvalDecideRefused*` sentences in all eleven packs and seven derived `approvalNoApproverHoldingSlots2..8` per pack. The precedent for adding keys to this same catalog is a3381cccbc (#36450), which declared `Clause-②: no`. `messages.ts` is not reachable from the package `exports` entry (`src/index.ts` re-exports none of it). The narrowed TypeScript annotation on the per-locale pack constants is internal.
- **J5. Messaging notice payload: right.** A notice for 2 to 8 slots now emits a new message id with keyed `typeN` / `valueN` params. One slot, and more than 8 slots, keep their earlier ids and shapes. The literal English body is unchanged, which is pinned through the real `NotificationTextRenderer`. `@objectstack/service-messaging`'s keyed-param contract does not move.
- **J6. Console readers: consumer-side reads, right.** `refusalBodyUserMessage` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/flowResponse.ts`) reads the envelope's `error.userMessage`, else a flat body's top-level `userMessage`. Both go through one `declaredUserMessage` predicate, the same two members the client lifts. The inbox `humanizeError` shows a marked refusal before the generic line. Consumer reads of an existing contract are `Clause-②: no` by precedent c13af73039 (#36440). See F2 for the changeset coverage.
- **J7. Metadata protocol: `none`, right.** No author-writable key, value or type changes, and the diff touches no `packages/spec/src/**` path.

### ② Semver level

- **Levels:** `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` and `@objectstack/rest` is right. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3 says a non-protocol change, widening or not, ships `patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **F1 (must-fix): `Clause-②: no` is wrong; it must read `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.** J1 adds a member to the approvals door's published response body. Under execution-duties.md's Clause ②, widening an accept set or enlarging a public surface is `yes`. The repository has declared this exact kind of change `yes (widening)` every time:
  - 62d9d0d998 (#34619): this same door gained `userMessage` (and `innerRefusal`) on `RESUME_FAILED`. `@objectstack/rest` patch, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.
  - 568d41642b (#34304): the `/data` 409 and its row errors gained a `userMessage` key, declared `yes (widening)`.
  - a8126d244d (#35811): the REST batch refusal body gained `failedOperation`, declared `yes (widening)`.

  The only nearby `no` precedent is e17c2ae1a3 (#36581). It changed the language of an existing `userMessage` and added no member, so it does not cover this head. The PR's own changeset says the door now answers "with `userMessage` at the top level ... on every mapped row" where it answered none before, which describes a widening. landing-operations.md calls a wrong `no` "an auditable false declaration". **Fix:** rewrite the line in three places: the PR body, the changeset body (`.changeset/36463-no-approver-text-in-reader-language.md`), and the card's claim line, which is the carrier the Clause-② queue gate reads. The changeset's "The REST door" bullet already describes the widening and can stay. The level stays `patch`.
- **F2 (should-fix): the changeset omits `@object-ui/app-shell`.** The diff changes `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/flowResponse.ts`, but the changeset names `@object-ui/console`, not `@object-ui/app-shell`. Every earlier change to this file named `@object-ui/app-shell`: c13af73039, 5bca14fc24, b3572509b9, 9da2f4b095 and f7ff693c46. The package is private, but `privatePackages.version` is `true`, so it is versioned and its CHANGELOG is compiled from changesets. **Fix:** add `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`. `Check Changeset` is green, so the gate does not catch this omission.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`:** empty. Nothing to answer.
- **Deviations (dev report 7122061191):**
  1. Two console readers changed instead of one. **Accepted.** Both are "the console reader that shows the decide refusal". The shared `type: 'api'` reader is gated by the same predicate the client applies, so no unmarked text gets promoted.
  2. The PM's producer-pattern assumption was corrected (`lockedError` / `snapshotQueryRefusal` rather than the `recognisedRefusal` block). **Accepted.** It was a third-zone assumption, and the correction holds against the code.
  3. The PM's flatten-into-one-param route was falsified, and derived arity sentences capped at 8 replace it. **Accepted.** The falsification is reasoned against `NotificationTextRenderer`'s one-text-or-one-hole-free-key holes. The cap is a declared constant, and the shape over 8 is unchanged from `main`.
  4. `userMessage` is also set on the another-approver branch. **Accepted.** One refusal never reads half-localized, and the card's Acceptance (entirely Chinese in zh-CN) is served by it. It enlarges the producer set behind F1's widening and adds no separate surface.
  5. Two `wip:` commits are in the history. **Accepted.** History only, with no contract effect.
- **`out_of_scope_findings`:**
  - More than 8 slots still names its slots in English. **Accepted as a recorded deviation.** It is in the PR's Acceptance notes and matches `main`'s behaviour for every multi-slot notice. Removing it needs a list-shaped keyed param in `@objectstack/service-messaging`. Whether to file a follow-up card is the seat's call under filing-gate.md.
  - Bulk approve reports failures by title only. **Accepted.** It is pre-existing and was observed, not introduced here. Filing is the seat's call.
- **SQL push-down:** no finding. The diff adds no id materialisation and no in-app join. `notePositionLabels(slatePositions(...))` is the existing label read, still reached only when no one else is on the slate. The derived sentences are built at module load.
- **Author:** the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed.
- **Prior rulings on the edited lines:** all three hold. Option B (the override never approves its actor's own request) is kept. The #13807 stranded envelope still spreads last. The 2026-08-31 anchored strip is unchanged.

Findings: **F1 must-fix**, **F2 should-fix**. Because of F1 the verdict is FAIL. Once F1 and F2 are fixed, only the declaration text and the changeset front matter change. The original reviewer then reads that delta.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-36463-no-approver-text-in-reader-language`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufziwMkZG34d69p8BHb4`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `a6c6666adee23afc20e585b0cc95a3fea78c0ed1`
Local-runs: none

Delta round on the previous record for head 869d5de0a (F1 and F2). Inputs read:
- card #36463: everything in round 1, plus the claim amendment 7122541004 and the round-2 and round-3 dev reports 7122558196 and 7122608140;
- the updated PR #36846 body, including its "Widened door response (Clause-②)" section;
- the net diff `origin/main...a6c6666ad`. `git diff 869d5de0a a6c6666ad` touches only `.changeset/36463-no-approver-text-in-reader-language.md` (+4 / -1), so every code file is byte-identical to the head judged in round 1;
- the check-runs on this head, read at 05:07Z: 35 runs, of which 8 success, 10 skipped and 17 in progress, with none failed. The successes include `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `PR-body guards`. Build, type-check, lint and test are still in progress. Round 1's head was all green on the same code. Landing still waits for full green on this head, which is a landing check and not part of this verdict.

Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

The code is unchanged, so round 1's J1 to J7 stand as judged.
- **J1, the approvals REST door's wire body.** Handlers for nine routes (`approve`, `reject`, `recall`, `revise`, `resubmit`, `reassign`, `remind`, `request-info`, `comment`) share `handleApprovalError`. On every mapped row, its flat `{ code, error }` refusal body gains an optional top-level `userMessage` when the thrown error carries a marking. The only in-tree producers are the two `403 FORBIDDEN` decide refusals of a submitter's own approval. This widens a public surface, and it is now declared that way (see ②).
- **J2 to J7** are unchanged:
  - J2: the thrown error gains `userMessage`, and `message` stays byte-identical.
  - J3: no new error code.
  - J4: the new catalog keys follow precedent a3381cccbc.
  - J5: messaging payload ids for 2 to 8 slots, and the English body is unchanged.
  - J6: the console reads the body as a consumer.
  - J7: `Metadata-protocol: none`.

### ② Semver level

- **F1: closed.** All three carriers now read `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: the changeset body, the PR body, and the card's claim amendment 7122541004 (a line-initial key, "was `no`"). This matches the same-door precedent 62d9d0d998 (#34619) and the REST-body precedents 568d41642b (#34304) and a8126d244d (#35811). `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` and `@objectstack/rest` stays right for a non-protocol widening with `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **F2: closed.** The changeset front matter now names `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch` for `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/flowResponse.ts`. That matches c13af73039 and the four earlier changesets for that file.
- **F3 (nit): the new changeset paragraph states the widened scope too narrowly.** The paragraph "Widened door response" says "The approvals decide door ... gains one optional member" and "Two rows answer it today". Two points are off:
  - The member rides every mapped row of all nine approvals routes that share `handleApprovalError`, not only the decide door.
  - Both refusals answer through one mapping row (`FORBIDDEN`). What the paragraph counts as two rows are two producers.

  The bullet below it in the same entry ("The approvals routes answer ... on every mapped row") states the full scope correctly, so the CHANGELOG entry still declares the whole widening. The PR body's section has the same wording. Optional fix in prose: "the approvals routes (`approvals-routes.ts`) gain ... ; two refusals produce it today, both on the `403 FORBIDDEN` row".
- **F4 (nit): the PR body's "What changes" line is stale.** It still lists the changeset as "patch for `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/rest` and `@object-ui/console`", without `@object-ui/app-shell`. This is PR-body prose only: the shipped changeset is right.

### ③ Boundary flags
